---
title: "Tech Value: model and leaderboard"
subtitle: "What was tried, how it was tested, and whether it beats the naive baseline"
---

```{python}
import plotly.express as px
from IPython.display import Markdown

from pdi import site

board, meta = site.load("tech-value", "leaderboard")
holdout, hold_meta = site.load("tech-value", "holdout")
folds, fold_meta = site.load("tech-value", "folds")
coef, coef_meta = site.load("tech-value", "coefficients")
verdict = hold_meta.get("verdict") or {}
automl = meta.get("automl")
```

## Result

```{python}
#| output: asis
if not verdict:
    print(site.empty_state(hold_meta, "Model result"))
else:
    print(f'::: {{.verdict}}\n**{verdict["statement"]}**\n\n'
          f'Holdout error (mean absolute error in log score): baseline '
          f'{verdict["holdout_mae_log_baseline"]:.3f}, picked model '
          f'{verdict["holdout_mae_log_picked"]:.3f}. Improvement '
          f'{verdict["holdout_improvement"]:.3f} against a fold-to-fold spread of '
          f'{verdict["fold_spread"]:.3f}.\n\n'
          f'Published model: **{verdict["published_model"]}**.\n'
          f'{site.finding_line(verdict.get("finding"))}:::')
```

The test, written before any result was seen: a model trained on older processor generations
must predict the newest generation better than a **cores-times-clock baseline**, by more than
the spread between time-ordered folds. If it does not, the baseline is published and the page
says "no signal found".

```{python}
#| output: asis
if verdict:
    c = meta["counts"]
    print("| Period | Processors first available | Results | Processors | Used for |\n|---|---|---|---|---|")
    print(f'| Train | before {meta["valid_start"]} | {c["train"]["results"]:,} | {c["train"]["processors"]:,} | fitting every model |')
    print(f'| Validation | {meta["valid_start"]} to {meta["holdout_start"]} | {c["validation"]["results"]:,} | {c["validation"]["processors"]:,} | ranking models and making the pick |')
    print(f'| Holdout | from {meta["holdout_start"]} | {c["holdout"]["results"]:,} | {c["holdout"]["processors"]:,} | one score, after the pick |')
```

## Holdout: the newest generation

Scored once, for the baseline, the plain regression and the single model the leaderboard
picked. The leaderboard below is not the result; this table is.

```{python}
if not holdout.empty:
    display(Markdown(holdout.assign(published=holdout["published"].map({True: "Yes", False: ""}))
        [["model", "n_results", "mae_log", "median_abs_pct_error", "published"]]
        .rename(columns={"model": "Model", "n_results": "Results", "mae_log": "MAE (log score)",
                         "median_abs_pct_error": "Median abs. error %", "published": "Published"})
        .to_markdown(index=False, floatfmt=".3f")))
```

## Leaderboard (validation period)

Every model tried, ranked on the validation period. The naive baseline is always a row.

```{python}
if not board.empty:
    cols = {"rank": "Rank", "model": "Model", "mae_log": "MAE (log score)",
            "median_abs_pct_error": "Median abs. error %", "n_results": "Results"}
    if "fit_time_s" in board.columns:
        cols["fit_time_s"] = "Fit time (s)"
    display(Markdown(board[list(cols)].rename(columns=cols).to_markdown(
        index=False, floatfmt=".3f", missingval="")))
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
if not board.empty:
    if automl:
        print(f'AutoGluon {automl["autogluon_version"]} last trained on {automl["trained_at"][:10]} '
              f'with the `{automl["preset"]}` preset, a {automl["time_limit_s"]}-second limit, '
              f'on CPU, over {automl["n_spec_results"]:,} results. It retrains weekly, not on every run.')
    else:
        print("AutoGluon has not been trained yet. The leaderboard shows the baseline and the "
              "plain regression only until the weekly training job has run.")
```

## Fold-to-fold spread

Expanding-window folds inside the period before the holdout. Each fold trains on everything
earlier and tests on the next block of processors. The standard deviation of the improvement
column is the noise level the holdout improvement has to clear.

```{python}
if not folds.empty:
    display(Markdown(folds.rename(columns={
        "fold": "Fold", "train_until": "Trained on processors before", "n_train": "Train results",
        "n_test": "Test results", "baseline_mae_log": "Baseline MAE", "plain_mae_log": "Plain MAE",
        "improvement": "Improvement"}).to_markdown(index=False, floatfmt=".3f")))
```

## The plain regression

The ranking of over- and under-performers uses this model, not the AutoML winner, because
every term in it can be read. The AutoML score only shows how much signal the plain model
leaves behind. Features are in logs, so the coefficient on `log_cores` is an elasticity: the
percentage change in score for a one percent change in core count.

```{python}
if not coef.empty:
    display(Markdown(coef.rename(columns={"term": "Term", "coefficient": "Coefficient",
        "std_error": "Std. error", "p_value": "p-value"}).to_markdown(index=False, floatfmt=".4f")))
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
if not coef.empty:
    print(f'R² {coef_meta["r_squared"]:.3f} on {coef_meta["n_results"]:,} results, fitted on all '
          f'periods for description only. The standard errors treat results as independent, '
          f'which they are not (many results share a processor), so they are too small.')
    print(site.finding_line(coef_meta.get("finding")))
print(site.source_note(meta))
```
